target_customer: Banked and unbanked consumers and small businesses in francophone West Africa, mainly Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal
problem: Fewer than 25 percent of people in francophone Africa are banked and traditional banks are costly.
business_model: Digital bank with interchange, card and premium tier fees, lending and business payments

founders.name: Regis Bamba
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by TechCrunch Apr 2025 (spelled Regis Ba in one place and Bamba later); not on YC page

competitors.name: Wave
competitors.what: Low-cost mobile money in Senegal and Cote d'Ivoire

competitors.name: Orange Money, Moov Money, MTN MoMo

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile banking app with card issuing through partner banks and KYC; regulation and partners were harder than code.

defensibility.rationale: Partner-bank cards, a 2025 microfinance approval and 1M+ users help, but Wave and telcos entered prepaid cards.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wave launched a prepaid Visa card and Axian moved into the segment by mid 2025 per LaunchBase Africa; Djamo responded with credit and a microfinance licence.

market_need_then: Company and TechCrunch cite under 25 percent banked in francophone Africa and over 55 percent of Djamo users unbanked.

branding.brand_signature: Prepaid Visa card with instant opening

brand_strength.rationale: 1.5M claimed users and a 4.7 rating over 71K reviews on its site, plus TechCrunch and Jeune Afrique coverage; no source on name or visual identity.

outcome_analysis: Djamo reached over a million active customers in Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal, raised a 14 million Series A in 2022 and a 17 million equity round in April 2025, and gained a microfinance approval. Telcos and Wave are pressing on its prepaid card turf, and a Series C near 40 million was reported in July 2026, so the trajectory is strong but contested.
notes: Series B stage is labelled other because TechCrunch calls it the latest equity round; a launchbaseafrica headline calls it post Series B, and one source lists a separate $13M Series B in Nov 2024, unreconciled. A $3.5M debt facility (Oct 2025) appears only on StartupList, unverified. Investor list of the Series A comes from a secondary report. Competitor entries cite 2025 and 2026 sources, so they are later observations of rivals that existed in 2020 and 2021, not dated at the batch. Company launched Nov 2020 per search results. Name origin not found.
